adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Replacing live SET keys with ZSETs makes rolling deployments fail with Redis WRONGTYPE against unexpired buffers or old writers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a change from Redis SET operations (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to ZSET operations (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py. During a rolling deployment, old code instances would still use SET commands while new instances use ZSET commands on the same Redis keys. Redis will return WRONGTYPE errors when SET commands are executed against ZSET keys or vice versa. The keys have TTLs (set_timeout) so unexpired buffers from old writers would cause failures. This is a real deployment compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 silently splits sufficiently deep trace trees into incorrect segments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the loop limit being reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 in add-buffer.lua line 30. The original comment explicitly states 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1,000, trace trees with depth between 1,000 and 10,000 that were previously handled correctly will now be silently split into incorrect segments. This is a real correctness issue - the code change directly reduces the supported depth of trace trees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Writing spans before the separate script-side eviction lets a concurrent queued flusher consume an unbounded segment after the read-side span limit was removed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in buffer.py, the read-side span limit check (max_segment_spans) was removed from _load_segment_data (lines 446-452 deleted). The Lua script add-buffer.lua now enforces a 1000 span limit via zpopmin eviction, but this happens after spans are written. The finding correctly identifies a race condition: if a flusher reads the segment between when spans are written (zadd at line 197) and when the Lua script's eviction runs, it could consume more than 1000 spans since the read-side limit was removed. This is a valid concurrency concern where the write and eviction are not atomic with respect to concurrent readers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10,001 to 1,001 nodes leaves deeper span trees unjoined and can flush one trace as separate incomplete segments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the loop limit being reduced from 10000 to 1000 in add-buffer.lua line 30. The original comment stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1000, span trees with depth between 1001 and 10000 that were previously handled correctly will now fail to be joined properly. This is a real behavioral change that could cause trace data to be incomplete for deep span trees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The new fixed 1000-span eviction limit bypasses the existing `max_segment_spans` setting, leaving a public buffer configuration knob dead and the limit duplicated across language boundaries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a hardcoded limit of 1000 in the Lua script (line 62: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)`). Looking at buffer.py, there is indeed a `max_segment_spans` configuration that was previously used (the diff shows removal of code that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`). The finding correctly identifies that the Lua script now enforces a fixed 1000-span limit that doesn't respect the Python-side `max_segment_spans` configuration, creating a configuration inconsistency. This is a legitimate architectural concern about duplicated/inconsistent limits across language boundaries, though not a bug per se since the limit still functions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — OptimizedCursorPaginator` copies nearly all of `BasePaginator.get_result`, so future cursor fixes will need to be kept in two implementations that can silently diverge.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912 in paginator.py) duplicates most of the logic from BasePaginator.get_result. Looking at the diff, the new class copies the cursor handling, queryset building, hit counting, offset calculation, and result processing logic. This is a legitimate architectural concern - if bugs are fixed in BasePaginator.get_result, they would need to be manually applied to OptimizedCursorPaginator as well, creating maintenance burden and risk of divergence. This is a real, specific, diff-grounded concern about code duplication that could lead to future maintenance issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — No test inserts over 1000 spans with distinct end timestamps to verify eviction retains the intended newest spans.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new span eviction mechanism in add-buffer.lua (lines 55-62) that uses zpopmin to remove spans when count exceeds 1000, keeping the ones with highest scores (newest by end_timestamp_precise). This is new, nontrivial logic. Looking at the test files in the diff, none of the test cases add more than a handful of spans - they all add 4-6 spans at most. The finding correctly identifies that there's no test verifying the eviction behavior works correctly with >1000 spans. This is a legitimate missing test coverage concern for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:72 — No endpoint test exercises the opt-in paginator against audit-log datetimes, leaving its incompatible cursor key conversion undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new OptimizedCursorPaginator class and adds code to use it in the audit logs endpoint when 'optimized_pagination=true' is passed. The finding correctly identifies that there are no tests added for this new pagination path in the audit logs endpoint. Looking at the diff, the OptimizedCursorPaginator uses get_item_key() which does math.floor/ceil on the key value, but DateTimePaginator (the original) handles datetime fields differently. The test files modified in the diff are for spans/buffer functionality, not for the audit log endpoint pagination. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added functionality.
